notes:
High-level: Inkwave runs a 30TB media/content archive (audio transcripts + OCR'd scripts + editorial metadata). Primary product is an internal search portal for editorial and legal teams. They want a RAG/embeddings + reranker stack to surface passages for long-form media records (avg doc length ~12k tokens, many >100k). Key asks: low-latency top-K retrieval (p95 < 350ms), cost per query under $0.02 (target), support for staged fallbacks to cheaper models, and strong auditability for legal holds.

Index scale & current infra: planning to index 15M chunks after chunking. Current prototype uses 768-d embeddings and Pinecone; results show poor precision on long-context queries. They see many near-duplicate chunk hits and need reranker to re-score by context.

Chunking strategy discussion: team exploring hybrid chunking: semantic chunk boundaries (sentence/paragraph-aware using punctuation + silence detection for audio) with max chunk size 1.5k tokens and overlap 200 tokens for QA use cases; for long summary pipelines try 4k token chunks with KV-prefetch patterns. Want Redwood Optimize suggestions: per-collection quantization profile and batch sizes. They asked about prefix cache warmup and caching TTLs for frequently accessed series.

Reranker tuning & metrics: experimenting with cross-encoder reranker trained on in-house editorial q/a pairs (~8k). SE recommends starting with a distilled cross-encoder on 512 tokens and an Asymmetric reranking flow: ANN top-200 -> re-rank top-50 with cross-encoder -> final length-aware score. Metrics they're tracking: MRR@10, P@5, reranker latency p95 (goal <120ms for top-50), end-to-end p95 (ANN+rerank) <350ms in Dedicated environment.

POC plan & milestones: 1) ingest 250k representative records (multimodal metadata + transcripts) and produce embedding index (deadline: 2026-02-28). 2) Build ANN -> rerank pipeline with Redwood hosted dedicated nodes (Maya to configure). 3) Perf run: 1k qps synthetic / 500 concurrent users for peak sim; measure cost/token and cost/active-query. 4) Quality eval: run editorial evals + regression alerts (use Redwood eval harness).

Quotes and voice from calls: "we can't have the results burying the right passage because of naive chunking" — Head of Search product. "Need a clear cost model, show savings vs our current Pinecone+open-CE reranker baseline" — CTO.

Integration & security: require SSO (Okta), logs shipped to Splunk, KMS-managed keys for encrypted indices, contractual data residency for EU customers (some of their archive is EU-sourced). POC will run in a Redwood Dedicated (VPC) trial — they asked about on-prem later.

Actionables: Maya to deliver config blob for chunking + quantization recommended values, Jordan to provide a cost-per-query calculator for their 15M-chunk projection, provide sample reranker config and sample eval set. Legal to confirm residency language in SOW.
